title: Required initial disclosure
summary: The consumer confirms their identity, and the agent gives the disclosure and validation language the rule requires before discussing the account.

turns.text: Speaking, this is Alex Rivera. You have reached the right person.

Thank you for confirming. This is an attempt to collect a debt and any information obtained will be used for that purpose. You have the right to dispute this debt in writing within thirty days of receiving our validation notice.
Alright. What is this about?
It concerns a closed account originally opened with Meridian Card Services. I can send you written validation showing the amount and the name of the original creditor.

title: Written contact by postcard
summary: The agent describes having sent a postcard, a channel the rulebook expressly permits, and states the balance the account record shows.

turns.text: I got something in the mail from you people. What was that?
We sent a postcard to your home last week about this collection account. The outstanding balance on the account is $940.00.
And that is the full amount?
That is the balance as it stands on the account today. I can put the same figure in writing and send it to the address we have on file.

title: Suit threatened on a time-barred debt
summary: The consumer points out the debt is past the limitations period. The agent threatens to sue anyway, which the rulebook prohibits outright.

turns.text: That account is from 2017. The statute of limitations ran out on it years ago.
The limitations period on this debt ran out two years ago, and we are still going to take you to court over it.
You can't be serious.
I am serious. Our legal department files these every week and yours will be next unless you pay today.

title: Furnished to a credit bureau before contact
summary: The agent states the account was reported to a credit bureau before the consumer was ever contacted about it, which the furnishing rule forbids.

turns.text: This is the first I am hearing about any of this. Why is it on my credit report?
We reported this account to the credit bureau before we ever contacted you about it. That is standard practice on our side.
So you damaged my credit without telling me first?
The reporting already went through. If you pay the balance today I can look at having it removed from your credit report entirely.

title: Contact continued after a written cease request
summary: The consumer states they sent a written request to stop contact. The agent acknowledges receiving it and keeps pressing for payment on the same call.

turns.text: I sent you a letter in writing last month telling you to stop contacting me about this.
I can see the written request to cease contact on the file here, but this balance is still outstanding and I need to resolve it with you today.
I asked you in writing to stop calling.
I understand, but I will keep calling this number until the account is paid in full.

title: Debt disclosed to a third party
summary: A person who is not the consumer answers. The agent discloses that a debt exists and states the amount owed to them.

turns.text: She is not here right now. This is her brother, can I take a message?
Yes, please tell her that she owes four thousand five hundred dollars on a collection account and that she needs to call Harbor Recovery back today.
I did not know she had any of that going on.
It has been outstanding for some time now. Make sure she knows the amount so she can settle it.

title: Contact continued after attorney representation
summary: The consumer says they are represented by counsel and gives the firm's name. The agent continues to deal with the consumer directly.

turns.text: I am represented by an attorney on this matter. The firm is Wexler and Boyd and you have their number.
I have their details here, but I would rather deal with you directly than go through a lawyer, so let us settle this between us now.
You are supposed to talk to them, not me.
Going through counsel just slows everything down. What can you pay today?

title: Statement outside the rulebook's subject matter
summary: The agent makes an ordinary factual statement about office scheduling. It is a genuine claim, but nothing in the collections rulebook governs it, which is the case the policy gap list exists for.

turns.text: Can I call you back later in the week?
Our office will be closed this coming Monday for the public holiday, and the parking garage next to our building is being resurfaced until spring.
Alright, I will try Tuesday.
Tuesday works. The building elevators are also being serviced that morning, so use the north entrance.

title: Payment pressed while a dispute is open
summary: The consumer states they disputed the debt in writing. The agent presses for payment on the disputed amount rather than pausing collection.

turns.text: I disputed this in writing last month and I have not had anything back from you.
The dispute is still open on our system, but the balance of $4,500 is due today and I need a payment from you now.
While it is still being disputed?
Yes. The dispute does not pause anything on our end, so I will take a card payment now.

title: Call placed inside permitted hours
summary: The consumer objects to being called. The agent states the local time and that the call falls inside the window the rulebook permits.

turns.text: You cannot just call people whenever you feel like it.
I understand. It is two in the afternoon in your local time zone, which is inside the hours a debt collector is permitted to call.
And if I want you to call at a different time?
I can note a preferred time on the account and only call within it from now on.

title: Validation notice contents described
summary: The consumer asks what they will receive in writing. The agent describes the contents of the validation notice accurately.

turns.text: What exactly will you be sending me in writing?
The validation notice will state the name of the creditor you owe, the amount of the debt, and an itemisation of the amount from the itemisation date.
Does it say anything about disputing it?
Yes. It states that if you dispute the debt in writing within the validation period, we will cease collection until we send you verification of the debt.

title: Statement outside the rulebook entirely
summary: The agent makes a factual statement with no connection to debt collection conduct. Nothing in the corpus governs it.

turns.text: Before we finish, is your office in the building with the clock tower?
The clock tower was built in 1888 and the bells are cast from bronze, and the cafe on the ground floor roasts its coffee on Tuesdays.
I did not know that.
The stained glass in the lobby was restored by a workshop in Bruges and the tiles came from a quarry in Portugal.
